solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Child brings home some works of Shakespeare

parts.note: a son is a child
to net is to bring home, as in netting a profit

explanation.surface: A child comes home from school carrying a few volumes of Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brings home' reads as carrying something into the house; here it means earns, as a salary nets a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Shakespeare wrote 154 fourteen-line poems of this kind, a small part of his output.

clue.text: Rest matters when dancing for savvy American

indicators.note: dancers move about the floor and change places, so the letters change places too

parts.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

explanation.surface: Someone insists that taking breaks matters to a dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective: 'savvy American' means shrewd, in an American idiom, not a savvy person.
explanation.definitionFit: An American coinage for the shrewdness learned on city streets rather than in school.

clue.text: Five seen in Christmas story

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it

parts.note: Noel is Christmas
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone spots the number five in a Christmas tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christmas story' reads as one phrase, but Christmas is wordplay and 'story' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a book-length work of prose fiction is a story.

clue.text: Basic tools of hostile criminal

indicators.note: a criminal is bent, crooked, and bent letters are pushed out of their order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A description of the crude weapons carried by an aggressive crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hostile criminal' looks like an adjective and noun; criminal is the anagram signal and hostile the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Crudely chipped flints once taken for the earliest human tools, so tools of the most basic kind.

clue.text: Run faster than anyone else on final part of lap, correct?

parts.note: running faster than anyone ever has puts your time in the books
the home straight is the last stretch of a lap

explanation.surface: A question about a runner breaking a record on the home stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue looks like athletics; only the last word, 'correct', is the definition, and it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to put right a false account of events is to correct it.

clue.text: Weirdly, I curtsey for bouncer?

definitions.note: a bouncer is one example of security staff, hence the question mark

indicators.note: something done weirdly is done strangely, so the letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: Someone admits to an odd curtsey offered to the doorman at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: A bouncer is the doorman who keeps out troublemakers at a club or pub; the question mark says he is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the doorman at a club is part of the staff who keep the place safe.

clue.text: Attached new structure briefly to support component of wheel

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower part holds up the one above

parts.note: a spoke is part of a wheel
N = new
FORT, a structure, cut short

explanation.surface: Instructions for fitting a new part beneath a wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attached' looks like assembly language, as in bolted on, but it means in a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone already in a relationship is taken, attached to a partner.

clue.text: Henry visits small restaurant for bit of cereal

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside the place visited

parts.note: a caff is a cheap British café
H = henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry drops in at a café for a bite of breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: A caff is British slang for a cheap café. The surface wants cereal to be breakfast; it is the grain crop.
explanation.definitionFit: The husks threshed away from wheat or other grain are one part of the cereal plant.

clue.text: Payments from magnificent matches

parts.note: royal = magnificent, fit for a king
cup ties are matches

explanation.surface: A football club earns money from some grand fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: A tie is a knockout match in British football, as in an FA Cup tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Sums paid to an author or rights holder each time a work is sold or used.

clue.text: Wearing jewellery, returned to island

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: a letter addressed to someone opens with Dear
an ait is a small island in a river

explanation.surface: A bejewelled traveller comes back to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To island' has to be read as the address on a letter, which would begin 'Dear Ait'. An ait is a small island in a river such as the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing a tiara, the jewelled crown-like band, so wearing jewellery of one kind.

clue.text: Tell school to accept fool

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone is told to report their school for admitting an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' is the verb to tell on someone, to inform, not to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for informing on someone, as a child tells on a classmate.

clue.text: Recalled nut gathering as most poor

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, a fan
a fest is a gathering, as in a beer fest

explanation.surface: Nuts collected in a poor harvest are being recalled.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for tacky or poor quality. 'Nut gathering' suggests squirrels; nut is an enthusiast here.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang superlative: the most tacky or shoddy, so the poorest in quality.

clue.text: Trump picked up seaweed close to major battle site

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word up makes it read bottom to top

parts.note: trump is British slang for breaking wind
an alga is a seaweed

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so the last letter of major

parts.note: last letter of major

explanation.surface: A politician collects seaweed near a great battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants Donald Trump; in British slang to trump is to break wind. 'Major' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The cape off south-west Spain where Nelson beat the French and Spanish fleets in 1805.

clue.text: Material had rewrites to be edited

indicators.note: editing moves words about, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

explanation.surface: Some written material needed several rewrites before editing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' pretends to be written copy, which the rewrites and editing support; it is cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A woollen cloth handwoven in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland, so a material in the fabric sense.

clue.text: The making of modern America is raw?

definitions.meaning: the straight reading: the conflict that created the United States
the setter's reading: RAW is what you get by turning a three-letter word round, so the answer describes it

explanation.surface: A question whether the founding of modern America was a crude business.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, WAR made revolutionary, turned round, and it produces RAW, which is what the clue shows.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1775 to 1783 war in which the American colonies won independence from Britain.

clue.text: Attachment on the side and centre of safe light

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: middle two letters of sAFe
fair = light, as in fair hair

explanation.surface: A description of a lamp fitted to the side and middle of a safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attachment on the side' reads as a fitting; it is a romance conducted on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: An extramarital romance: an emotional attachment carried on beside a marriage.

clue.text: We set such homophones very indiscriminately at the moment of truth

indicators.note: things set indiscriminately are put down with no regard for order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 20 letters; very gives V

explanation.surface: A crossword setter confesses to scattering sound-alike clues about at random.
explanation.walkthrough: V is the standard abbreviation for very. 'Homophones' is fodder, not a signal to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the point when a decision can no longer be put off.

clue.text: Lie on the counter to receive constant acclaim

indicators.note: counter means against the usual direction

parts.note: a tale is a lie, as in telling tales
c is the constant for the speed of light

explanation.surface: A shop assistant fibs at the counter to win praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a shop counter; it is the reversal signal. C, the speed of light, is a standard constant.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for brilliant success and the applause that greets it.

clue.text: Cautious man would add petrol, perhaps, to have energy earlier

indicators.note: the E, standing for energy, is to be placed earlier in the phrase than it was

parts.note: a man would add petrol, perhaps, as he'd fuel, giving HE'D FUEL

explanation.surface: A careful man topping up with petrol so that he has energy sooner.
explanation.walkthrough: HE'D FUEL has its E moved: 'to have energy earlier' takes the E of FUEL forward to sit straight after HE, so DFUE becomes EDFU.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heedful pays attention to warnings and risks, which is what being careful means.

clue.text: Jew somehow has to know one welcoming extreme characters

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so the letters go inside
somehow means in some way or other, so the letters of has are rearranged

parts.note: to ken is Scottish and northern English for to know
I is the Roman numeral for one
A and Z are the letters at the two extremes of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone told they must get to know a person who is welcoming to extremes.
explanation.walkthrough: To ken is to know, in Scots; the A and Z sit just before the final I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashkenazi Jews are those descended from the Jewish communities of central and eastern Europe.

clue.text: Periodically, Spain asks to get rid of repellent type

indicators.note: at regular periods, so take every other letter: SpAiN aSkS

parts.note: alternate letters of SpAiN aSkS

indicators.note: something repellent drives others back

parts.note: to fire is to get rid of, as a worker

explanation.surface: Every so often Spain asks to be rid of an off-putting kind of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repellent type' reads as an unpleasant person; repellent is the reversal signal and type means typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: A family of typefaces whose letters lack the small finishing strokes called serifs.

clue.text: Old reactive metal found in new entrance hall

parts.note: N = new
an atrium is an entrance hall

explanation.surface: A chemical discovered lying about in a newly built lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' looks like a signal to hide something inside; it only links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The former name for sodium, a highly reactive metal, which is why its symbol is Na.

clue.text: Smile ahead of fellow's progress

parts.note: a grin is a smile
a don is a fellow of a college; the 's is 'is', joining to the definition

explanation.surface: A grin foreshadows a colleague's advance.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb for moving forward slowly and relentlessly, a laborious kind of progress.

clue.text: Ring during post-mortem; morgue upset

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the answer lies within the words
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: post-morTEM; MORGue, read backwards

explanation.surface: A ring turns up during an autopsy and the mortuary is in uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: The morbid words are only letters; read backwards through 'mortem; morgue'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber or metal ring that lines a hole, so a ring of a practical kind.

clue.text: Competent drunk

definitions.meaning: a well-drilled band or crew is said to be this
an old slang word for drunk

explanation.surface: A verdict on someone who is capable despite being inebriated.
explanation.walkthrough: The competent sense is as in 'we run a tight ship', or a band that plays tightly together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are informal: well drilled and precise, and the old slang for drunk.

clue.text: While contracted, husband is welcomed by singer

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by a host is taken inside

parts.note: an alto is a singer
H = husband

explanation.surface: During the engagement, the husband-to-be is welcomed by a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' means shortened: the answer is a clipped although, and although can mean while. The surface makes it a marriage contract.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal short spelling of although, which in 'while I agree' means while.

clue.text: Conquest stops fantastic snog speedily

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so the word goes into the gap in the anagram
fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters of snog are rearranged

parts.note: a conquest is a win

explanation.surface: A romantic conquest cuts short an amazing kiss, and quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges SNOG as ONGS, and 'stops' plugs WIN into it. A snog is British slang for a long kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on wings is an old poetic idiom for moving swiftly, as if flying.

clue.text: Plant essential work by little sister

parts.note: core = essential, as in core subjects
OP is short for opus, a work
sis is a shortened sister

explanation.surface: A reminder that the vital gardening was done by a younger sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb telling you to plant something; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like garden flower, often yellow, also called tickseed.

clue.text: Rest of lake going into Ouse, it's said

indicators.note: something going into another ends up inside it
said aloud, so Ouse is heard as ooze

parts.note: Ouse sounds like ooze, and to ooze is to seep
L = lake

explanation.surface: Water from a lake flows into the River Ouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in England, said like ooze; the synonym seep then takes the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the body's nightly rest.

clue.text: They deliver and drive growth

parts.note: UPS, the parcel company, delivers
an urge is a drive

explanation.surface: A courier firm's slogan about delivering and driving the economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They' is the parcel firm UPS; 'drive' is a noun, as in sex drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden rise or increase, a burst of growth.

clue.text: Less drunk, retrospectively screen missing diamonds for bishop

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking back, so the result is read from the end
missing means the letter for diamonds goes from the word
for means the letter for bishop takes its place

parts.note: a reredos is the ornamental screen behind a church altar
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A drunk is told to look back and see the screen, with no diamonds but a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing diamonds for bishop' changes REREDOS into REREBOS, and 'retrospectively' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober means not drunk, so the comparative describes someone less intoxicated than another.

clue.text: Triggers people sampling flagellation, according to Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner is the byword for swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: flagellation is whipping, so the word whip
people sampling things are triers

explanation.surface: Something sets off people trying out a whipping, a bizarre scene.
explanation.walkthrough: In WHIP TRIERS the sounds W and TR swap places to give TRIP WIRES, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripwire is a wire stretched low so that touching it sets off a trap, alarm or explosive.

clue.text: Fight a bit

definitions.meaning: informal for a brawl or scuffle
a small leftover piece, as of paper

explanation.surface: An admission of fighting a little.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'a bit' as a noun, a fragment, not as 'slightly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are nouns: an informal word for a fight, and a small leftover piece.

clue.text: Station surrounded by multitude of buses ignoring old lady with hungry dog

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out

parts.note: a computer's main circuit board carries many buses, the lines that carry data
O = old, dropped from MOTHERBOARD
a hub is a station, as in a transport hub

explanation.surface: A bus station scene, with an elderly woman and a starving dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Buses here are computer circuits, not vehicles. 'Old' also looks like part of 'old lady'; it is the dropped O.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme woman who went to the cupboard for a bone and found it bare, so her poor dog had none.

clue.text: Work to protect old city with millions in trouble

indicators.note: a protector wraps around what it guards

parts.note: toil is work
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
M = millions

explanation.surface: Efforts to defend an ancient city with a fortune fail in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, in ancient Mesopotamia, is the crossword's standard old city.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of great disturbance and confusion, trouble in its widest sense.

clue.text: Bedlam at Eurovision entertains enthusiast

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside, so the phrase holds the answer within it

parts.note: bedlAM AT EURovision

explanation.surface: Chaos at the Eurovision Song Contest delights a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: Eurovision is the annual European song contest, famous for its chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: From Latin amator, a lover: someone who does a thing for love of it rather than pay.

clue.text: Fuss around small guitar beginning to rile manager

parts.note: ado is fuss
mini = small
a Strat is a Fender Stratocaster guitar

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of rile

explanation.surface: A fuss over a little guitar begins to annoy the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fender Stratocaster is known to players simply as a Strat.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one who runs the affairs of an office or organisation.

clue.text: A group playing popular covers start to shout "Get out while you can!"

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

indicators.note: covers means wraps round, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: on means playing, as an act is on stage
hip means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: start to takes the first letter of shout

parts.note: the first letter of shout

explanation.surface: A band playing pop covers starts to shout at the crowd to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' has ONHIP wrap round S, the 'start to shout', giving ONSHIP after A and BAND. The music words make 'covers' look like cover versions.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandon ship is the order to leave a sinking vessel, an urgent command to escape.

clue.text: Able to produce young almost immediately, taking care when cavorting

indicators.note: taking means holding, so the anagram is put inside
almost means nearly all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: pronto means immediately

indicators.note: cavorting means leaping about, so the letters of care are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who can have babies almost straight away, taking care when frisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims PRONTO to PRONT, and 'taking' holds CREA, the letters of CARE rearranged by 'when cavorting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Procreant is an old adjective meaning generative, capable of breeding offspring.

clue.text: Doctor nearly agreed to break glass appliance

indicators.note: to break something is to split it open

parts.note: a tumbler is a drinking glass
DR = doctor
YES, agreed, nearly complete

explanation.surface: A doctor almost consented to smashing a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glass appliance' looks like a unit; glass is the wordplay and appliance alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A household machine that dries laundry in a heated rotating drum.

clue.text: Mentor drives a buggy

indicators.note: buggy software is faulty, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A mentor takes the wheel of a small cart.
explanation.walkthrough: Buggy is a vehicle in the surface and the anagram signal in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a trusted guide who gives counsel.

clue.text: Investigative team deputy's motor vehicle

parts.note: a vice is a deputy, as in vice-president; VICE'S
a quad is a quad bike, a four-wheeled motor vehicle

explanation.surface: A police unit uses the deputy's car.
explanation.walkthrough: Vice as a noun means a deputy; the 's joins it to the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: The police unit that investigates crimes such as prostitution, drugs and gambling.

clue.text: Maybe it starts to cause enmity, say

parts.note: the word it is one example of this part of speech

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: first letters of cause and enmity

explanation.surface: A remark that something might be the start of bad blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is not a vague thing but the word it, and 'maybe' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to utter a word, or to declare aloud.

clue.text: Switch positions to suppress outspoken notices when business is slow

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down and keep in, so the switch positions keep the other pieces inside

parts.note: a switch has two positions

indicators.note: spoken out, so the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: notices = sees, which sounds like seas

explanation.surface: Staff switch jobs to hide candid notices while trade is quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch positions' looks like a job swap; it is the two settings of a light switch.
explanation.definitionFit: The quiet months of a resort or trade, when custom falls away.

clue.text: Cage, perhaps, reportedly containing metal

indicators.note: as reported by word of mouth, so the name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: the actor Nicolas Cage; his first name is what you hear

explanation.surface: A cage said to hold metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Cage is the actor Nicolas Cage, and 'perhaps' says he is one example of a Nicolas.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist's adjective for compounds holding nickel, a metal.

clue.text: Ambassador covered in strange nasal discharge

indicators.note: a thing covered in something is wrapped in it

parts.note: rum = strange, odd
HE = His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A diplomat is spattered with some odd mucus.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is old British slang for odd. An ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, HE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for the watery fluid that runs from the nose and eyes.

clue.text: Oblivious about introduction of cream in coffee

parts.note: deaf = oblivious, as in deaf to advice

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of cream

explanation.surface: Someone does not notice cream being added to their coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the link, not a container signal; 'about' does that work.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for decaffeinated coffee, the kind with the caffeine removed.

clue.text: Female to entice inspiring former partner in turn

parts.note: F = female

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: to lure is to entice
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A woman lures back her ex, taking her turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' looks like praise for the ex; read it literally as breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical word for a bend or curve, so a turn in the shape of something.

clue.text: Country cops following archangel

parts.note: Israel is a country
F = following, as in pp. 5f.

explanation.surface: A nation's police follow an angel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cops' is a verb meaning catches, not police.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic tradition, the archangel who will sound the trumpet on the Day of Judgement.

clue.text: I'm surprised time interrupts count again

parts.note: Really! is what you say when surprised
T = time

explanation.surface: A surprised official stops the clock to count the votes again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm surprised' stands for a one-word exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefixed verb: a tally is a count, and the prefix re- adds the again.

clue.text: Irishman drinks red liquid in church

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so the anagram goes inside the name

parts.note: Cathal is an Irish man's name

indicators.note: liquid means flowing and unfixed, so the letters of red are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Irishman knocking back red wine inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Cathal is a common Irish forename, which is all 'Irishman' tells you; the drinking surface points at wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, containing the bishop's throne.

clue.text: Burst in and blushed, having forgotten wife takes ecstasy

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out
to take something in is to hold it

parts.note: to blush is to go red: went red
W = wife, dropped
E = ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A man burst in and went red, having left his wife, high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Blushed has to be expanded into two words, WENT RED, before anything can be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bursting in is a forceful way of going in, and the past tense matches.

clue.text: Shelter from sunshine, suffering with temperature

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, knocked about, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
T = temperature, added to the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone seeks cover from the sun because of a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a British prefabricated corrugated-iron hut from the First World War, like an American Quonset hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-cylinder of corrugated iron used for troops and stores, a shelter of the plainest kind.

clue.text: Fast, say

definitions.meaning: high-speed, as a train or delivery that makes no stops

explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example'; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for high-speed service and a verb for putting thoughts into words.

clue.text: Singer? Just beat it!

definitions.note: the question mark signals that the singer is a songbird

parts.note: to pip is to beat narrowly
it as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells a performer to get lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat it' looks like 'go away', but the split falls between beat and it. To be pipped at the post is British for being narrowly beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown songbird of fields and moors, so a singer in the bird sense.

clue.text: In rows, leading European leaves exhausted

parts.note: tiered = arranged in rows, like seats
the first letter of European, E, departs

explanation.surface: A European front-runner walks off, worn out, from a crowd in rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: worn out and in need of rest.

clue.text: More fully developed American departing to make amends for going north

indicators.note: someone departing goes away, so the A goes from the word
north is up the page, so in a down clue the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: to repair a wrong is to make amends for it
A = American, removed to leave REPIR

explanation.surface: An American who is leaving heads north to make up for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going north' only works because this is a down clue: the letters climb the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of ripe, used of fruit or plans that have come further to maturity.

clue.text: Call to account as takings at a higher level

parts.note: a haul is the takings, as from a robbery
up = at a higher level

explanation.surface: Auditors demand an explanation as the revenue rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Account' and 'takings' push a bookkeeping reading; the definition is a British idiom for making someone answer for their conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom: to drag someone before a court or superior to answer for their conduct.

clue.text: Technique used for A Shot in The Dark?

definitions.text: Technique used for A Shot in The Dark?

parts.words: Technique used for A Shot in The Dark?
parts.note: the surface reading: the 1964 Pink Panther comedy starring Peter Sellers; the setter's reading: taking a picture where there is no light needs a burst of artificial light

explanation.surface: A film buff asks how the Pink Panther comedy was made.
explanation.walkthrough: A Shot in the Dark is a Pink Panther film, but read literally it is a photograph taken in darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: The technique of lighting a subject with a brief bright burst at the moment of exposure, which makes a dark shot possible.

clue.text: Trudged along, slightly overweight?

explanation.surface: Someone plods along, a bit heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second sense as a jokey euphemism for plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: walked steadily on foot, and cushioned with a little extra flesh.
